claims.statement: Persistent obstructive swallowing symptoms require structural and mucosal assessment; endoscopy can inspect narrowing and obtain esophageal tissue.
claims.limitation: Choice depends on the clinical phase; suspected proximal pouch and acute perforation use different pathways.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: A negative biopsy does not close a suspicious stricture evaluation; cross-sectional imaging or EUS and repeat biopsy can be needed when the clinical or endoscopic findings still suggest cancer.
claims.limitation: One direct guideline; low-certainty evidence. Preserve the negative result within the tissue actually sampled. No empirical false-negative percentage or mandatory sampling device.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Evaluation for EoE requires at least six esophageal biopsies spanning at least two levels, including when the mucosa appears unremarkable.
claims.limitation: Numeric sampling minimum directly verified; samples from stomach/cardial tissue do not satisfy esophageal territory. No biopsy count by itself diagnoses EoE.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Symptoms of esophageal dysfunction together with a peak biopsy count of at least 15 eosinophils per high-power field and assessment of competing causes support EoE.
claims.limitation: High-power-field area varies; use the pathology laboratory standard. Constructed counts are observations, not newly asserted probabilities.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Dilation treats EoE-associated narrowing and is used with continuing anti-inflammatory therapy rather than as a substitute for disease control.
claims.limitation: Medication and diet options can be valid; no universal budesonide-versus-PPI ranking, dose or failure interval is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Symptoms, endoscopic findings and esophageal histology contribute to treatment assessment; easier swallowing after dilation does not establish histologic remission.
claims.limitation: The case with histologic remission supplies actual adequate follow-up biopsies; treatment effects are not inferred from symptoms alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: An empiric elimination diet is an EoE treatment option; currently available allergy tests should not determine the elimination foods for EoE.
claims.limitation: This concerns EoE, not management of immediate IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. A least-restrictive initial milk-elimination trial is supported; no universal superiority over medicines or more extensive diets.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Mechanical abrasion at a food-bolus impaction site can confound inflammatory histology, so suitable esophageal samples should come from other sites.
claims.limitation: Single adequate consensus publication for the precise trauma-site boundary. Does not justify ignoring a suspicious lesion at that site.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: A stenosis or focal mucosal lesion suspicious for neoplasia at food-bolus endoscopy warrants targeted biopsy to assess malignancy.
claims.limitation: Original focal observations must support suspicion; ordinary extraction abrasions are a different target.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Some swallowed bones are poorly seen on radiographs; a negative film does not exclude a retained esophageal bone.
claims.limitation: No exact sensitivity or claim that all bones are radiolucent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: CT is appropriate when a swallowed foreign body may have caused perforation or another complication requiring intervention.
claims.limitation: Do not generalize to routine imaging before every uncomplicated nonbony food-bolus extraction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: A sharp-pointed object retained in the esophagus requires emergent therapeutic endoscopic removal even when the patient can handle saliva.
claims.limitation: Urgency is supported; no fixed gameplay wait or numerical clinical removal deadline is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Failed retrieval, extraluminal migration, proximity to vital structures or perforation can require operative foreign-body management rather than further luminal extraction attempts.
claims.limitation: One direct guideline. Approach depends on object location, contamination and tissue viability; no universal incision or extraction protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: CT with appropriate contrast assessment can identify esophageal perforation and its extraesophageal extent; a normal chest radiograph does not exclude the injury.
claims.limitation: The exact CT protocol is determined by the hospital team; an aspiration-prone completely obstructed patient is a different oral-contrast context.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: A stable patient with early, contained esophageal disruption, minimal contamination and expert surveillance may be managed nonoperatively in hospital.
claims.limitation: One adequate direct guideline, low-certainty evidence. This excludes uncontrolled sepsis, freely leaking contamination and unmonitored outpatient observation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Nonoperative perforation care includes withholding oral intake, antimicrobial treatment and nutrition support with close reassessment and drainage of collections when indicated.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; exact antibiotic selection and duration are not settled and are not authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: For a free thoracic perforation with viable reparable tissue, operative source control can include debridement, reinforced primary repair and adequate drainage.
claims.limitation: One direct primary guideline. Destruction, diseased esophagus or inability to repair changes the role of resection or diversion; no universal rule for every leak.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: After adult caustic ingestion, loss of esophageal wall enhancement on contrast CT raises concern for full-thickness necrosis and can support emergency surgery.
claims.limitation: One direct guideline. A technically adequate contrast study and clinical assessment are necessary; normal vital signs and absence of free gas do not by themselves establish viable wall.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Long, angulated, multiple or caustic esophageal strictures are high-risk dilation contexts in which fluoroscopic guidance improves procedural control.
claims.limitation: One direct guideline, moderate-certainty guidance. No novel diameter increment, mandatory number of sessions or fixed post-injury timeline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Selected refractory benign esophageal strictures can receive a temporary fully covered removable stent after other approaches fail; uncovered or partially covered stents can embed.
claims.limitation: Not first-line treatment for an ordinary untreated stricture. No claim that stenting always beats incision, further dilation or surgery; candidate assumes specialist selection for a removable stent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Fluoroscopic contrast swallowing can demonstrate a proximal pharyngoesophageal pouch and its dynamic relationship to regurgitation or aspiration.
claims.limitation: Single direct guideline for the new mapping; existing frozen PASS retains its original independent evidence and approval history.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Flexible endoscopic septum division is an established option for symptomatic Zenker diverticulum and can avoid the neck-extension limitations of rigid endoscopy.
claims.limitation: One adequate direct guideline. Flexible-first preference is weak/low certainty; no universal superiority over open surgery and no ranking against modern Z-POEM.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Multiple biopsy-supported distant metastases from esophageal cancer generally call for a systemic oncologic treatment strategy rather than a definitive plan limited to the primary and regional nodes.
claims.limitation: One adequate accessible government professional evidence summary. Does not specify a drug regimen or rule out selected local palliation; the candidate has multiple hepatic deposits, not an oligometastatic exception.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with multiple confirmed hepatic deposits matching an esophageal squamous carcinoma.

claims.statement: A positive horizontal endoscopic-resection margin without submucosal invasion or other high-risk histology can be managed through local endoscopic surveillance or re-treatment.
claims.limitation: One direct society guideline. The candidate supplies visible residual local tissue, making re-treatment the offered local plan; this is not a general rule to observe all positive margins.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Lymphovascular invasion or deep submucosal invasion after endoscopic esophageal cancer resection makes local clearance insufficient; full staging and additional oncologic treatment, including surgical consideration in selected fit patients, are warranted.
claims.limitation: One direct society guideline. Additional treatment is selected through multidisciplinary clinical assessment; the candidate completes distant staging and selects a fit patient. No exact nodal probability, universal esophagectomy mandate or ranking against every chemoradiation strategy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: An embedded partially covered esophageal metal stent can be removed using a fully covered stent placed inside it as a staged endoscopic technique.
claims.limitation: One directly verified society guideline recommendation 8. Exact device, dwell interval and operative escalation depend on specialist assessment; none is invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a partially covered esophageal stent embedded at its uncovered ends without a complication requiring primary surgery.

claims.statement: EUS-guided needle acquisition can obtain tissue from an esophageal wall process when smooth overlying mucosa has yielded negative forceps biopsies.
claims.limitation: BSG supports repeat investigation after CT/EUS in suspicious negative strictures. The needle-acquisition route is supported by a selected observational cohort, with no universal diagnostic-yield or comparative-superiority assertion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: CT with intravenous enhancement and swallowed water-soluble contrast can assess a suspected postprocedural esophageal leak and associated mediastinal or pleural abnormalities.
claims.limitation: ESGE directly specifies oral water-soluble contrast and WSES supports contrast-enhanced CT/CT esophagography. No dose, universal protocol or categorical exclusion of fluoroscopic esophagram is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Purely diagnostic re-endoscopy has a selected role in suspected esophageal perforation because instrumentation can extend a defect or spread contamination.
claims.limitation: One directly verified position statement supports the caution. Specialist re-endoscopy remains appropriate for selected unresolved questions or planned endoscopic therapy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: For an appropriate visible superficial esophageal neoplastic lesion within scarred or fibrotic tissue, expert endoscopic submucosal dissection is a supported resection approach.
claims.limitation: ESGE 2023 gives a weak, low-certainty ESD recommendation for scarred/fibrotic areas derived from ESGE 2022. A positive lateral margin alone does not establish that every case requires this technique.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Visible Barrett-associated neoplastic lesions should be resected before ablation of appropriate remaining flat Barrett epithelium.
claims.limitation: These are related ESGE guideline publications, with shared evidence rather than independent validation. The field-treatment comparison stays subordinate to the early-cancer lesion decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Flexible and rigid esophagoscopy are complementary retrieval approaches, with rigid access considered for selected upper-esophageal objects or airway and access problems.
claims.limitation: WSES provides low-certainty guidance. It does not establish a unique procedure ranking from upper location alone. This claim supports the reason for parking the attempted route question.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Negative mucosal forceps samples or a superficial resection do not by themselves establish the nature of a process centered deeper in the esophageal wall.
claims.limitation: One observational publication supplies the directly verified compartment discussion. It does not prove that every smooth stricture is malignant or that all deeper sampling techniques have equal performance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

claims.statement: Covered esophageal stents can provide luminal diversion across selected iatrogenic wall defects, including defects unsuitable for direct clip closure or incompletely closed defects.
claims.limitation: Stent use is selected by defect features, stability, drainage and specialist expertise. These sources do not establish a universal stent-versus-surveillance ranking for every contained leak.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly constructed esophageal clinical context

limitations: No official examination frequency, blueprint percentage or proprietary examination corpus was used. Testing relevance is editorial.
Several emergency and procedural boundaries have one adequate primary guideline only; each claim marks that limit.
ACG highlights and ACG full guideline describe one publication. WSES mirror pages and duplicated DOI records are not independent sources.
All substantive claims and all proposed content await exact named clinical review.

Round 2 added three directly accessible primary publications. NOM selection is low-certainty and patient-specific. Covered-stent guidance does not establish a universal ranking over surveillance. Scar-specific ESD guidance is low-certainty and shares evidence with ESGE 2022. The EUS acquisition series is selected and observational.
The CC BY-NC-ND article is used for independently written facts. NC and ND restrictions are explicit, with no copied or adapted expression.
All seven parked version-2 attempts remain excluded from active proposal exports. Mappings retain the original reviewed versions and parked attempts for auditability.
